summary: Hero episode on American programmer and activist Aaron Swartz, who helped build RSS, Creative Commons and Reddit, fought for open access and against SOPA, and died by suicide in 2013 while facing federal prosecution over JSTOR downloads.

evidence.note: Birth in 1986 near Chicago and childhood with early home computers
Joins the RSS working group in August 2000, first major contribution
Lessig gives him his first job coding Creative Commons; extended segment on Lessig's ideas
Stanford year and disillusion with university life
JSTOR downloads at MIT in 2010-2011 lead to arrest
Federal prosecutor brings felony counts under computer and wire fraud laws
Long segment on Quinn Norton's grand jury cooperation and its consequences
Lobbying Congress and founding Demand Progress to defeat SOPA
Legacy to 2023: open access policy changes, Sci-Hub, Aaron's Law, MIT report

notes: No theme fits copyright and open access, or chronic illness and mental health, which are both central; tech-internet is the closest primary. electoral-politics covers the SOPA congressional fight and his political ambitions, a moderate fit. Quinn Norton's birth year is not given, so floruit is used.
